standard_prerequisites.name: Conductor of the integral closure of a one-dimensional semi-local domain
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows descending from the integral closure back to B_i after raising x to a power.

standard_prerequisites.name: Characterization of Dedekind domains by discrete valuations
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the discrete valuations v_i used in the induction.

core_obligations: Reduce to the case where each B_i is integrally closed: if x^{-1} lies in the Jacobson radical of the integral closure B_i' then a power of x^{-1} lies in B_i by the conductor lemma, and since Spec(B_i') -> Spec(B_i) is surjective the same holds in the Jacobson radical of B_i (proof lines 7546-7553).
Reduce to the local case: replace a non-local B_i by the finite collection of its local rings (B_i)_m, which are discrete valuation rings (proof lines 7555-7559).

Reformulate with discrete valuations v_i : K -> Z, so that the task becomes finding a nonzero x in A with v_i(x) < 0 for all i, and treat the case r = 1 by the surjectivity hypothesis (proof lines 7561-7570).

Run the induction for r > 1: take x with v_i(x) < 0 for i < r by induction, assume v_r(x) >= 0, find nonzero y with v_r(y) < 0 by the base case, replace x by a high power so that v_i(x) < v_i(y) for i < r, and verify that x + y has all the required negative valuations (proof lines 7572-7578).
proof_roadmap: Pass to integral closures and then to discrete valuation rings.
Translate the Jacobson radical condition into negativity of finitely many valuations.
Prove the valuation statement by induction, combining two elements whose valuations are ordered.
Conclude with the base case coming from the surjectivity hypothesis.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for a domain A with fraction field K and finitely many Noetherian one-dimensional semi-local domains B_i inside K whose tensor products with A surject onto K, an element x of A whose inverse lies in the Jacobson radical of every B_i. The proof first replaces each B_i by its integral closure, using the conductor lemma to descend back after raising x to a power, then replaces semi-local Dedekind domains by their local rings, and finally reformulates the problem in terms of the associated discrete valuations v_i: one must find a nonzero x in A with v_i(x) < 0 for all i (proof lines 7546-7566). The existence is then proved by induction on the number of valuations, with the crucial step replacing x by a power so that v_i(x) < v_i(y) for i < r and taking x + y (proof lines 7568-7578). H2: the reduction chain and the weighted induction combining two elements are the non-routine content.
